Accurate, real-time monitoring and forecasting capabilities are foundational to modern grid operations. Without upgraded systems that can process vast amounts of data and predict renewable generation patterns, grid operators cannot effectively manage the variability and complexity of today’s distributed energy landscape. 2.3 Transportation System Devices 2.3.1 Environmental Monitoring The transportation system is affected by the environment, and it can affect the environment itself. Therefore, environ- mental monitoring is included in many traffic applications. • Air quality sensorsplay an important role, especially in metropolitan areas. Both the environment (wild- fires, high pollen counts, high ozone) and the transportation system (emissions) can result in low air quality. Many metropolitan areas issue air quality alerts asking drivers to minimize driving, and advising medically vulnerable populations to minimize exertion and time spent outdoors. • Fog Sensors: Fog and smoke can lead to dangerous low-visibility conditions on roadways. In areas where naturally occurring very dense fog can be extremely dangerous, fog sensors have been deployed. In 1990, dense fog led to a deadly car pile-up of 99 vehicles on I-75 near Calhoun, Tennessee (Local 3 News 2015). These sensors, along with a human-in-the-loop (state trooper assigned to this area), were put in place to trigger fog gates to shut down the highway when extremely low visibility necessitates it. • Weather Sensors: During inclement conditions, some autonomous vehicle functions may be deactivated; e.g. dynamic cruise control and lane assistants, which depend on distance sensors and camera-based lane detec- tion. For legacy vehicles and (partially) autonomous vehicles alike, the loss in traction can pose a safety issue. Infrastructure can also be affected by snow and rain. Camera-based traffic sensors rely on good visibility to function. Many northern US regions have infrastructure to shut down highways during major snow storms us- ing snow gates, similar to fog gates. Depending on place- ment, they could simply be installed for public safety. However, if placed strategically, they can support traffic operations. For instance, cameras placed along highways can be used by traffic operation centers for real-time traffic monitoring (Brogan and Berres 2023). Beyond this, they can also be used to obtain traffic counts and classify vehicles using object detection models such as You-Only-Look-Once (YOLO) (Zhang, Liang, and Wang 2025).
